newsitem.title: ITALY: Edison shares slip, results disappoint.
newsitem.headline: Edison shares slip, results disappoint.

text.p: Shares in Italian energy company Edison slipped on Wednesday, in contrast to other shares in the Montedison-Compart grouping, after 1996 Edison preliminary results came in below analysts' estimates, dealers said.

At 1320 GMT, Edison shares slipped 1.66 percent to 9,970 lire after a day's low of 9,750 lire, while Montedison gained 0.68 percent to 1,324 lire and Compart was up 1.22 percent at 914 lire in a firmer Milan stock market.

"The gross operating margin of Edison was a little under estimates and sales slightly above. Therefore the actual margin on sales fell to 46.7 percent against an estimate of 50 percent, but it is not a big fall and the shares were trading very high," said analyst Paola Toschi at brokers Milla.

Montedison issued its preliminary 1996 results late on Tuesday, and of its four divisions only its energy interests grouped under Edison showed a rise in profits. Montedison controls over 60 percent of Edison, while Compart -- formerly Ferruzzi Finanziaria -- has around a 31 percent stake in Montedison.

Analyst Gianluca Codagnone of AFV Sim brokers put down the fall in Edison shares to the fall in margin as a percent of sales which was greater than estimates, while other figures within the whole grouping were in line with estimates.

In the results, Edison showed a 1996 gross operating margin of 880 billion lire and net sales of 1.881 trillion lire compared to estimates by the Milla analyst of 905 billion lire and 1.813 trillion lire.

According to a technical analyst, Edison shares were seeing a technical correction following a favourable upward trend. Edison shares reached a maximum of 10,975 lire on January 15 showing a rise of 67 percent from the minimum price in 1996 at 6,745 lire reached on January 2 1996.
